text:
A: Hi! Hi, sorry, can you hear me?
B: Yeah. Hiya.
A: I'm Megan. I'm in Chelmsford, in Essex.
B: Callum. Stockton-on-Tees.
A: Oh, nice. Erm, I've never been up north really. Well, I've been to Norfolk, but that's not north, is it? Sorry. That's east.
B: It's east, yeah.
A: Yeah. Erm, so are you working or at uni or...?
B: Uni. Final year, civil engineering. Teesside.
A: Oh, cool. I'm at uni as well, second year. Wildlife and conservation. So kind of the opposite, maybe? You build things and I go, please don't build on the newts.
B: Not really the opposite. My dissertation's drainage on new housing estates. Half of that's ponds now.
A: Ponds?
B: Yeah, sustainable drainage. SuDS. Instead of piping all the rainwater straight off, you put in swales and attenuation ponds so it holds back and soaks away slowly. Stops the flooding downstream. They're meant to be designed for wildlife and all that as well, but a lot of developers just do the bare minimum. Steep sides, a fence round it, grass mowed to nothing.
A: Oh, that's so interesting, honestly. We did pond dipping on one of those, I think, on a new estate near campus. It had loads of damselfly larvae in it. And the tutor said exactly that, that the edges need to be shallow so things can get in and out.
B: Yeah. Shallow margins. It's in the guidance, people just don't do it.
A: That's kind of annoying, isn't it?
B: It is, yeah.
A: Erm, so do you live in halls, or...?
B: At home. With my mam and stepdad. Saves paying rent.
A: That makes sense. I live with my boyfriend, in a li'le flat. It's tiny. We've got a guinea pig, you can maybe see his cage in the corner.
B: Right.
A: Sorry, I'm, erm, I'm rambling. Is that, is that alright?
B: It's fine.
A: Okay. Did you do the puzzle at the start? I ran out of time.
B: Did it. Last one took a while.
A: Same, I just stared at it. What do you want to do after you finish? Like, a job in drainage?
B: Drainage or highways. With a consultancy in the North East, ideally. Get chartered. Buy a house round home.
A: That's really sorted. I want to be a ranger, or an education officer with the wildlife trust, running sessions for kids. But I don't know if I'll get anything, do you know what I mean? There's not loads of jobs.
B: Volunteering helps, apparently. Lad on my course got on a placement that way.
A: Yeah, that's true. It's just hard when you've not got money to work for free.
B: Yeah. Fair.
A: Are you the first one in your family to go? To uni?
B: Yeah.
A: Me too. My mum's really proud but she doesn't really get what I do. She thinks I just look at birds.
B: My mam thinks I draw bridges.
A: Do you?
B: Not really. Mostly pipes.
A: I think we've nearly run out of time.
B: Yeah. Good luck with your course.
